chunks: They took their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah, son of Mary, and they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no god but He. Exalted is He above what they associate.
ai.seo_question: Who did the Jews and Christians take as lords besides God according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as highlighting how religious authorities (Ahbar) and monks (Ruhban) acquired the power to legislate Halal and Haram, effectively becoming lords alongside God by imposing their own rulings. It underscores the core Tawhidic principle that true worship is directed solely to Allah, contrasting this with the practical shirk of following human decrees as divine law. This concept is central to understanding the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Imams as the true interpreters of God's will.
